newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bills hold gains at close after RBNZ easing.
newsitem.headline: NZ bills hold gains at close after RBNZ easing.

text.p: New Zealand bank bill rates ended Thursday's session 20 basis points lower after a surprise easing in monetary conditions by the Reserve Bank.

Bank governor Don Brash said the bank had not moved its position from its monetary policy statement in December, but that in recent weeks the market had moved conditions to levels that were inappropriately firm.
The bank's economic projections for the next three years assumed the same mix outlined in the December MPS -- 90-day bank bills at 7.5 percent and the Trade-Weighted Index at 68.0.

The 90-day bank bill rate fell just over 20 basis points to 7.37 percent after the RBNZ's statement, while the New Zealand dollar dropped to US$0.7011/18 from 0.7049/56 just before the statement and 0.7054/61 at Wednesday's close.
The TWI fell to 68.66 from 69.04 before the statement and 69.13 at Wednesday's close.
The Kiwi dollar and the TWI kept slipping gradually, to finish the session at 0.7001/08 and 68.58 respectively.
However, the 90-days steadied at 7.37 percent, and dealers said that after an instantaneous reaction to the statement the market had hit a wall.
Corporate dealers had clients wanting to borrow into any strength, so interest to sell limited the rally.
"Basically the market sort of went "whoosh" when the numbers came through and they got something a little bit different from what they'd expected, but there was no follow-through," one dealer said.

"Certainly the enthusiasm of corporates to hedge in the swaps market under eight percent was very apparent in the two and three year area, and again the dealers hedged their books by selling some short dated bonds."
Dealers said sentiment was mixed, and there was some confusion about the longer term outlook given the uncertainty surrounding the achievability of the RBNZ's inflation forecasts.
Offshore trading overnight in the currency would determine where the short end opened up on Friday morning, dealers said.
Meanwhile, the longer end of the bond curve was still coming under pressure from offshore movements, with the 11/06 maturity ending a fraction weaker in line with U.S. weakness.

Bond spreads widened against the dollar bloc after a strong outperformance shortly after the statement. Mid bonds ended stronger against the U.S. and Canada but both mid and long bonds were outshone by Australia by the close.
